summary: Herzog's consultations ended on Nov 5 with a majority of incoming MKs recommending Eisenkot, while Likud, Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism backed Netanyahu and UTJ recommended no one. Herzog will name his choice on Sunday, Nov 8, citing mutual vetoes between and within the blocs. On Friday Liberman said in a post reported by the Jerusalem Post that he is willing to compromise on the Haredi draft law to join an Eisenkot-led coalition, and rejected a rotating premiership with Eisenkot. Yashar has rejected unity with Netanyahu, Shas still stands with Likud, and neither the Joint List nor UTJ has committed to backing an Eisenkot-led government.

phase.now: Herzog's consultations are complete; he is taking the weekend and will name his choice on Sunday, Nov 8
phase.next: Eisenkot is expected to receive the mandate, with 28 days to form a government plus up to 14 more; the new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he wants Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism in any future government and that the public does not want one dependent on Ra'am and the Joint List. Without a majority, he needs defectors or a new partner from the other side. On Nov 5 UTJ declined to recommend any candidate, leaving Netanyahu without its endorsements, while Otzma Yehudit recommended him. Likud's delegation, last to meet Herzog, urged him to give Netanyahu the mandate, the Jerusalem Post reports.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu and says he won't sit with him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Championed by Yair Golan, who met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29; the Times of Israel says he is the only Jewish-led bloc leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it. Channel 12 reports Abbas himself privately called an Eisenkot minority government with outside Arab support weak or impossible. AFP reports Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition relying on Arab parties, and the Joint List's Jabareen says he would back him from outside. A senior Joint List official told Walla on Nov 1 that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot to the president. Ynet reports Joint List and Ra'am leaders met in Nazareth on Nov 2 and will coordinate their recommendations. Ynet reports Bennett sides with Liberman against a government relying on Arab parties, believing it would collapse. On Nov 3 Golan met Joint List leaders and they agreed to keep coordinating, while the Times of Israel notes the bloc's joint statement gave no indication of how it would govern without Arab parties. On Nov 4 Ra'am announced it will recommend Eisenkot, while Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog a government cannot be formed with Arab parties. On Nov 5 the Joint List said it will recommend Eisenkot but will not formally join his coalition, offering possible outside support, Al Jazeera and ANI report. A Times of Israel analysis notes the Joint List has not said it will back an Eisenkot-led government.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot authorized examining a minority government with Ra'am inside and UTJ abstaining, possibly as leverage in unity talks; Yashar says such reports are not issued on its behalf. It falls short of 61 and Liberman rejects any government dependent on Arab or Haredi parties. Unnamed sources tell Ynet that Liberman berated Eisenkot at a Saturday meeting, saying the minority-government push hurt the bloc.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am and said on Nov 2 he would oppose an Eisenkot minority government.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it. A source close to Eisenkot tells Ynet he is trying to bring Shas and UTJ into a government he leads, naming Liberman as the main obstacle. A senior UTJ official told Ynet the party would offer Eisenkot the premiership for draft exemptions, which clashes with his national-service condition; Shas is reported to be out. Unnamed senior UTJ figures say the party might back an Eisenkot government from outside without a draft law first, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 2 Liberman declined to rule out cooperating with UTJ, saying the bloc will have to see what happens. Ynet reports on Nov 3 that Eisenkot is focusing on courting the Haredi parties and that Liberman has left the door open to talks on including them. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 3 that Shas and UTJ stress no decision has been made, with their rabbis due back around the start of consultations. On Nov 4 Shas recommended Netanyahu, and Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog it would not compromise key priorities to bring Haredi parties in, Ynet reports. On Nov 5 UTJ declined to recommend either candidate, with Goldknopf telling Herzog the party is not bound to any bloc, Ynet reports. ANI reports UTJ told Herzog its support for any government depends on legislation exempting yeshiva students from service. On Nov 5 Together told Herzog it will not accept a draft-evasion law, Israel National News reports. Channel 12 reports Liberman has dropped his refusal to sit with UTJ and that the opposition is in talks with it, but Yisrael Beiteinu told the Jerusalem Post it was not aware of this. Channel 12 reports the bloc is examining a coalition with UTJ and Shas, with draft talks starting from Liberman's 2018 bill, while Shas still stands with Likud. On Nov 6 Liberman said he is willing to be flexible and compromise on the Haredi draft law, the Jerusalem Post reports.

blockers.text: Haredi sources tell the Jerusalem Post that Deri won't join an opposition-led government without Likud.
Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman long pledged not to sit with Shas and UTJ, but on Nov 6 said he would compromise on the draft law.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.
Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog it rejects compromising security and economic priorities to include Haredi parties.
Together told Herzog it will not accept a law exempting Haredim from the draft.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ. Kan cites Netanyahu associate Benny Biton as saying Netanyahu wants unity, and an unnamed Likud official named Herzog and Trump as guarantors for Eisenkot. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point. Likud whip Ofir Katz told Army Radio the party opposes rotation and others can join the existing coalition. Channel 14 reports, citing unnamed sources, that Netanyahu has given up on unity talks and is preparing for a new election. Ynet reports Netanyahu told associates privately he is not ruling out any option, including rotation, and that Katz says unity is off if the opposition ousts Speaker Ohana. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he is open to a broad government with any party that does not support terrorism but that he should lead it; an associate told Ynet no unity proposal has yet been made. Israel Hayom reports a Likud source's assessment, not a negotiated offer, that Netanyahu could accept unity if he served about two years and then became president, with Eisenkot taking over. ANI, citing the Times of Israel, reports Shas Council of Torah Sages member Rabbi Moshe Maya urged a unity government. On Nov 5 Yashar's delegation rejected a unity government with Netanyahu and called him the obstacle to unity, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 5 Likud MK Yoav Kisch urged a broad national government and called on the opposition to end its boycott, the Times of Israel reports.

blockers.text: Likud whip Ofir Katz said the party opposes a rotation of the premiership.
Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation.
Channel 12 reports Liberman still refuses to join a Netanyahu-led government, even as he urges Eisenkot to.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.
Together MK Merav Cohen warned against a unity deal with Likud, saying "You don't make deals with scorpions."

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: Likud told Herzog on Nov 5 the mandate should go to Netanyahu and said relying on the Joint List would be dangerous, the Jerusalem Post reports.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: Yashar urged Herzog on Nov 5 to give Eisenkot the mandate, rejected unity with Netanyahu, and said it would negotiate first with its bloc partners.
red_lines: Partners must accept his four principles

רק.stance: Together recommended Eisenkot to Herzog on Nov 5, with faction chair Ginzburg vowing to help him form a government quickly and MK Merav Cohen rejecting both a draft-exemption law and a unity deal.
red_lines: No government reliant on Arab parties (per Ynet)

אמת.stance: The Democrats formally recommended Yashar leader Eisenkot to Herzog to form the next government on Nov 5, Haaretz reports.

ל.stance: On Nov 6 Liberman set out conditions for joining an Eisenkot-led coalition, saying he is ready to compromise on the Haredi draft law but rejecting a rotation with Eisenkot.

שס.stance: At its Nov 4 consultation Shas recommended Netanyahu, with MK Malkieli voicing hope for a coalition of at least 61 and saying the Council of Torah Sages fully backs Deri.

ג.stance: At its Nov 5 consultation UTJ, both Degel HaTorah and Agudat Yisrael, declined to recommend any candidate, with Pindrus saying they came to discuss issues, not people.

ב.stance: Otzma Yehudit recommended Netanyahu on Nov 5, and its delegation claimed without evidence that some votes were bought, Ynet reports.

ט.stance: Religious Zionism recommended Netanyahu on Nov 4, with its delegation arguing Arab nationalist parties are not legitimate partners in forming a government, Ynet reports.

עם.stance: Ra'am recommended Eisenkot to Herzog on Nov 5 and asked Speaker Ohana for an early vote on his successor, Ynet and the Times of Israel report.

ודם.stance: The Joint List announced a unanimous decision to recommend Eisenkot to Herzog, saying it will not formally join his coalition but may support it from outside, ANI reports.

timeline.text: Liberman laid out terms for joining an Eisenkot coalition, offering draft-law flexibility and saying rotation "must be consigned to oblivion."
After Herzog raised a unity deal, Yashar MK Shaul Meridor told him the public had sent the Oct. 7 government home, a Times of Israel analysis reports.
Herzog challenged Likud's Miri Regev for calling Eisenkot's camp a 'disaster bloc' while claiming to extend a hand.
Likud MK Yoav Kisch called for a broad national government of Zionist parties and urged the opposition to end its boycott and talk.
Channel 12 reports Liberman gave bloc partners a green light to negotiate with the Haredi parties, with draft talks based on his 2018 bill.
Herzog said the results may look clear but cited mutual vetoes between and within the blocs, and said he would hold personal talks with some party leaders before choosing on Sunday.
Herzog said Eisenkot received the most recommendations but that he will hand over the mandate only on Sunday, the Times of Israel reports.
Ra'am formally asked Speaker Ohana to hold a vote on his successor at the new Knesset's first session next week.
Likud's delegation, the last to meet Herzog, said the mandate should go to Netanyahu and warned against relying on the Joint List.
Yashar recommended Eisenkot, rejected a unity government with Netanyahu and said it would first negotiate with its bloc partners.
Channel 12 reports Liberman is now willing to sit with UTJ, ending his long-standing refusal.
Yisrael Beiteinu told the Jerusalem Post it was not aware of any change in Liberman's stance on Haredi parties.
Ynet tallies 67 recommendations for Eisenkot and 46 for Netanyahu once consultations ended, with UTJ backing neither.
Together MK Merav Cohen told Herzog the party rejects a draft-exemption law and warned against a unity deal with Likud.
Together recommended Eisenkot to Herzog, with faction chair Ginzburg pledging to help him form a government as quickly as possible.
dpa reports Herzog was due to meet Likud and Yashar on Thursday evening before deciding whom to task with forming a government.
Shas Council of Torah Sages member Rabbi Moshe Maya called a unity government the only solution, ANI reports citing the Times of Israel.
UTJ told Herzog its backing for any future government depends on legislation granting military-service exemptions, ANI reports.
The Joint List said it will not formally join an Eisenkot coalition but may support it from outside, to keep Netanyahu from returning.
The Joint List announced it will tell Herzog it recommends Eisenkot, which Al Jazeera says gives him a majority of recommendations.
The Democrats recommended Eisenkot to Herzog as the candidate to form the next government, Haaretz reports.
Opposition lawmakers demanded the Knesset speaker's removal, and he pledged a debate on the motion if a majority wants it, the Times of Israel reports.
UTJ told Herzog it recommends no one, Pindrus saying "We came to talk about issues, not people."
JFeed, citing Channel 12's Amit Segal, reports Otzma's party vote to recommend Netanyahu passed 19 to 7.
Herzog rejected Otzma's vote-buying claims as unsubstantiated, saying "There is no evidence or proof."
Otzma Yehudit recommended Netanyahu and claimed without evidence that some votes in the election were bought.
UTJ decided as a whole not to recommend anyone, and Goldknopf told Herzog the party is not committed to any bloc.
Ynet projects Eisenkot will receive more recommendations than Netanyahu, though still short of a 61-seat majority.
Al Jazeera, citing Channel 12, reports the Joint List is expected to coordinate with Eisenkot, endorsing him if asked or abstaining if he prefers.
Cassif told Anadolu the Joint List would likely recommend Eisenkot at its Thursday meeting with Herzog but was still deliberating.
